LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.weakTypicalSet: For an iid source p on a finite alphabet, the weakly ε-typical set at length n > 0 is the finite set of positive-probability words whose self-information per symbol differs from H(p) by strictly less than ε. At length zero the set is empty.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mem_weakTypicalSe: For an iid source p on a finite alphabet, a length-n word x is weakly ε-typical exactly when n > 0, its word probability P(x) is positive, and |−ln P(x)/n − H(p)| < ε.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.weakTypicalSet_ma: For an iid source p on a finite alphabet, the probability of any weakly ε-typical word of length n lies between exp(−n[H(p) + ε]) and exp(−n[H(p) − ε]), inclusive.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.card_weakTypicalS: The weakly ε-typical set at length n on a finite alphabet has at most exp(n[H(p) + ε]) words.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.prob_mul_exp_le_c: Let T be the weakly ε-typical set at length n for a finite-alphabet iid source p. Then |T| ≥ Pr(T) exp(n[H(p) − ε]), where Pr(T) is its iid probability.
